lessons.title: Get ready! What you will learn

pages.title: What you will learn
pages.body:
> 🔤 **Strand 2 — Algebra**
Using letters and symbols to describe patterns, relationships and unknown quantities.

> 🎯 **Content standard** (B8.2.2)
- B8.2.2.1 — Solve problems involving algebraic expressions (including multiplication of binomial expressions), factorise given expressions and substitute values to evaluate algebraic expressions.

> 🎯 **In this chapter you will learn to:**
- use the distributive property to remove brackets
- multiply two binomial expressions
- add, subtract, multiply and divide algebraic fractions
- substitute values into expressions, including fractions
- factorise expressions using common factors and grouping

pages.title: Key words and map
pages.body:
> ✨ **Key words**
- expand
- distributive property
- binomial
- algebraic fraction
- LCM
- substitute
- factorise
- common factor
- grouping

> 🗺️ **Sections in this chapter**
- 6.1 Expanding brackets
- 6.2 Algebraic fractions
- 6.3 Substitution
- 6.4 Factorisation

pages.title: Expanding brackets
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Use the distributive property to remove brackets and solve multiplication of binomial expressions.
Curriculum indicator B8.2.2.1.1
> 🔑 **Key idea: Distributive property** — **a(b + c) = ab + ac** and **a(b − c) = ab − ac**. Multiply **every** term inside the bracket by the term outside. A negative sign outside changes the sign of every term inside: −(p − q) = −p + q.
## ✏️ Example 6.1
Expand and simplify:
a) 6(x + 3) b) 2(6 − 5x) − 3(2 + 2x) − 4(3x − 1) c) −5x(3x + 4) d) 8 − (4 − d) − (6 − d) e) 3(x + 4) − 2(x − 5) f) (e + f − g) − (e − f + g)
**Solution**
a) **6x + 18**
b) 12 − 10x − 6 − 6x − 12x + 4 = **10 − 28x**
c) **−15x² − 20x**
d) 8 − 4 + d − 6 + d = **2d − 2**
e) 3x + 12 − 2x + 10 = **x + 22**
f) e + f − g − e + f − g = **2f − 2g**
## Multiplying two binomials
A **binomial** has two terms, e.g. (a + 2). To multiply two binomials, multiply each term of the first bracket by each term of the second bracket (four products), then collect like terms.
[[fig:m8-f19|Figure 6.1: Area model: (a + 2)(a + 3) = a² + 3a + 2a + 6]]
## ✏️ Example 6.2
Expand: a) (a + 2)(a + 3) b) (2x + y)(2x − y) c) (3x − 2y)(3x + 2y) d) (2x + 3)² e) (x − 2y)² f) (a + 2)²
**Solution**
a) a² + 3a + 2a + 6 = **a² + 5a + 6**
b) 4x² − 2xy + 2xy − y² = **4x² − y²**
c) 9x² + 6xy − 6xy − 4y² = **9x² − 4y²**
d) (2x + 3)(2x + 3) = 4x² + 6x + 6x + 9 = **4x² + 12x + 9**
e) (x − 2y)(x − 2y) = x² − 2xy − 2xy + 4y² = **x² − 4xy + 4y²**
f) **a² + 4a + 4**

pages.title: Keep going
pages.body: > ✨ **Did you know?** Results b) and c) are examples of the **difference of two squares**: (p + q)(p − q) = p² − q². Results d), e) and f) are **perfect squares**: (p + q)² = p² + 2pq + q².

pages.title: Exercise 6.1
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Exercise 6.1** — try these on paper or in your head, then tap **Quick check** to see the answers.
1. Expand: a) 4(2a − 7) b) −3(x − 2y + 5) c) 2p(3p + q) d) 5(m + 2) − 3(m − 4) e) x(x − 3) + 2x(4 − x)
2. Expand: a) (x + 4)(x + 5) b) (y − 3)(y + 7) c) (2m − 1)(m − 6) d) (3a + 2b)(a − b) e) (x + 6)(x − 6) f) (4k − 3)²
3. Show that (n + 1)² − n² = 2n + 1. Use this to find 51² − 50² quickly.

questions.q: Show that (n + 1)² − n² = 2n + 1. Use this to find 51² − 50² quickly.

pages.title: Algebraic fractions
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Perform addition, subtraction, multiplication and division of algebraic expressions including fractions.
Curriculum indicator B8.2.2.1.2
## Multiplying and dividing
Multiply numerators and denominators, cancelling common factors first. To divide, multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor.
## ✏️ Example 6.3
Simplify: a) [[2x/3]] × [[9/4x^{2}]] b) [[6ab/5]] ÷ [[3a/10]] c) [[x + 2/4]] × [[8/3(x + 2)]]
**Solution**
a) [[18x/12x^{2}]] = [[3/2x]]
b) [[6ab/5]] × [[10/3a]] = [[60ab/15a]] = **4b**
c) The factor (x + 2) cancels: [[8/12]] = [[2/3]]
## Adding and subtracting
Write each fraction with the **LCM of the denominators**, then combine the numerators. Put brackets round numerators with more than one term.
## ✏️ Example 6.4
Simplify:
a) [[a − b/3]] + [[3a/2]] b) [[2a/3]] − [[a − b/2]] c) [[5/6r]] − [[3/4r]] d) [[2x − 1/3]] − [[x + 3/2]] e) [[3a + 5b/4]] + [[a + b/8]] f) [[2x/6]] + [[2x − 3y/3]] − [[x + y/2]]
**Solution**
a) [[2(a − b) + 3(3a)/6]] = [[2a − 2b + 9a/6]] = [[11a − 2b/6]]
b) [[4a − 3(a − b)/6]] = [[4a − 3a + 3b/6]] = [[a + 3b/6]]
c) LCM of 6r and 4r is 12r: [[10 − 9/12r]] = [[1/12r]]
d) [[2(2x − 1) − 3(x + 3)/6]] = [[4x − 2 − 3x − 9/6]] = [[x − 11/6]]
e) [[2(3a + 5b) + (a + b)/8]] = [[7a + 11b/8]]
f) [[2x + 2(2x − 3y) − 3(x + y)/6]] = [[2x + 4x − 6y − 3x − 3y/6]] = [[3x − 9y/6]] = [[x − 3y/2]]

pages.title: Keep going
pages.body: > ⚠️ **Watch out!** In [[2x − 1/3]] − [[x + 3/2]] the minus sign applies to the **whole** second numerator: −3(x + 3) = −3x − 9, not −3x + 9.

pages.title: Substitution
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Substitute values to evaluate algebraic expressions including fractions and use these to solve problems.
Curriculum indicator B8.2.2.1.3
## ✏️ Example 6.5
If x = 2, y = −2, z = 3, c = 1 and d = −1, simplify where possible and then evaluate:
a) [[3/x + 1]] − [[2/x − 1]] b) [[1/x − 1]] + [[2/x + 1]] c) [[12xy/7]] × [[14x/20]] d) [[6x^{2} + 2xy/5z]] × [[15z^{2}/3x + y]] e) 5x + 7z² − 4d + 3y²
**Solution**
a) [[3/3]] − [[2/1]] = 1 − 2 = **−1**
b) [[1/1]] + [[2/3]] = 1[[2/3]]
c) Simplify: [[168x^{2}y/140]] = [[6x^{2}y/5]]; then [[6×4×(−2)/5]] = **−**[[48/5]] = −9.6
d) 6x² + 2xy = 2x(3x + y), so the expression = [[2x(3x + y)/5z]] × [[15z^{2}/3x + y]] = 6xz = 6 × 2 × 3 = **36**
e) 5(2) + 7(9) − 4(−1) + 3(4) = 10 + 63 + 4 + 12 = **89**

pages.title: Exercise 6.3
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Exercise 6.3** — try these on paper or in your head, then tap **Quick check** to see the answers.
1. If a = 3, b = −4 and c = [[1/2]], evaluate: a) [[a + b/c]] b) [[2a/b]] − c c) a² + b² − 4c d) [[ab/a − b]]
2. The formula A = [[1/2]](a + b)h gives the area of a trapezium. Find A when a = 7.5, b = 4.5 and h = 6.
3. If p = −2 and q = 5, evaluate [[p^{2} − q/q − p]] and [[3/p]] + [[2/q]].

pages.title: Factorisation
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Factorise given expressions involving the four operations and use the experiences gained to solve problems.
Curriculum indicator B8.2.2.1.4
> 🔑 **Key idea: Factorising** — **Factorising** is the reverse of expanding: write an expression as a product. **Common factor:** take out the HCF of all the terms, e.g. 6x + 9 = 3(2x + 3). **Grouping:** for four terms, group them in pairs, factorise each pair, then take out the common bracket.
## ✏️ Example 6.6
Factorise using common factors: a) 3ab + 6ac b) 54 − 81x c) 100x − 25x²
**Solution**
a) HCF = 3a: **3a(b + 2c)**
b) HCF = 27: **27(2 − 3x)**
c) HCF = 25x: **25x(4 − x)**
Check by expanding: 25x × 4 − 25x × x = 100x − 25x² ✓
## ✏️ Example 6.7
Factorise by grouping: a) 2ax + ay − by − 2bx b) ax − bx − ay + by c) 3x² + 2xy − 12xz − 8yz
**Solution**
a) Rearrange: (2ax + ay) − (2bx + by) = a(2x + y) − b(2x + y) = **(2x + y)(a − b)**
b) x(a − b) − y(a − b) = **(a − b)(x − y)**
c) x(3x + 2y) − 4z(3x + 2y) = **(3x + 2y)(x − 4z)**
## ✏️ Example 6.8
Use factorisation to evaluate quickly: a) 47 × 23 + 47 × 77 b) 8.6² − 1.4² (Hint: p² − q² = (p + q)(p − q))
**Solution**
a) 47(23 + 77) = 47 × 100 = **4,700**
b) (8.6 + 1.4)(8.6 − 1.4) = 10 × 7.2 = **72**

pages.title: Exercise 6.4
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Exercise 6.4** — try these on paper or in your head, then tap **Quick check** to see the answers.
1. Factorise: a) 12x + 18 b) 7p² − 21p c) 4a²b − 6ab² d) 15mn + 10m − 5m²
2. Factorise by grouping: a) xy + 3x + 2y + 6 b) pq − pr + 5q − 5r c) 6ab − 9a − 4b + 6 d) x² + 3x − xy − 3y
3. Evaluate using factorisation: a) 125 × 17 − 125 × 7 b) 99² − 1 c) 3.75 × 64 + 3.75 × 36

pages.title: Chapter 6 summary
pages.body:
- Expand: multiply every term inside the bracket; (a + b)(c + d) = ac + ad + bc + bd.
- (p + q)(p − q) = p² − q²; (p + q)² = p² + 2pq + q².
- Algebraic fractions: same rules as number fractions — use the LCM of denominators.
- Factorise by taking out the HCF, or by grouping pairs of terms.
